item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00089","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C15","C02","C23"],"selected_candidate_label":"C15","confidence":0.98,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C15 is the strongest reusable drafting template because it is an immediately preceding proclamation in the same supplementation series and supplies the child's distinctive recital framework, statutory grounding, two-part division between the general trade agreement and the exclusive Cuban agreement, and machinery for applying amendments and rectifications to earlier proclamations. C02 is also materially embedded in the child—the child expressly amends operative provisions first drafted there—but C15 more closely supplies the overall architecture of the later instrument. C23 is a related earlier iteration with substantially the same framework, though less complete than C15.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"Whereas, pursuant to the authority conferred by section 350 of the Tariff Act of 1930... on October 30, 1947 the President entered into a trade agreement with the governments of [the listed countries]...","parent_excerpt":"Whereas, pursuant to the authority conferred by section 350 of the Tariff Act of 1930... on October 30, 1947 the President entered into a trade agreement with the Governments of [the same listed countries]...","explanation":"The child substantially reproduces C15's lengthy, distinctive opening recital identifying the statutory authority, parties, GATT, Protocol of Provisional Application, and Final Act."},{"child_excerpt":"Part I Acting under the authority of said section 350... to the end that said trade agreement specified in the 1st recital... PART II To the end that said exclusive trade agreement specified in the 3rd recital...","explanation":"Both instruments use the same two-part operative architecture: Part I implements the multilateral agreement, while Part II separately implements the exclusive Cuban agreement."},{"child_excerpt":"including any amendments and rectifications of said agreement and said proclamation which have been proclaimed by the President, as if the rectifications... had appeared... on October 30, 1947","parent_excerpt":"including in each case any amendments and rectifications which have been proclaimed by the President... as though said rates, descriptions, and related paragraph numbers had appeared in part I of schedule XX... on October 30, 1947","explanation":"The child adapts C15's concrete legal machinery for retroactively integrating proclaimed amendments or rectifications into Schedule XX and the earlier proclamations."}]}
